info.title: SKU.io — Record a Purchase Invoice
info.description: Record a supplier's invoice (a bill / accounts-payable invoice) against a purchase order in SKU.io, from the invoice document itself — a PDF or email from the supplier — or from a plain description. Resolves the PO, maps the invoice's line items to PO lines and its freight/fee charges to the PO's financial lines, checks for duplicates by supplier invoice number, creates the purchase invoice, attaches the source document, and verifies the result with a three-way match. Can also record a payment against the invoice once one has actually been made.

get.summary: Find the purchase order the invoice bills. (The path is /list — a bare GET /api/purchase-orders is not a route and 405s.) Full-text search covers PO number, supplier name, item SKU, invoice number, and tracking number; filter[invoice_status] narrows to uninvoiced/partial/invoiced POs.

parameters.name: filter[search]
parameters.description: Search by the PO number printed on the invoice, or by supplier name. The param is filter[search] — a bare search= param is silently ignored and returns the unfiltered list. Narrow to a single PO before invoicing against it.

parameters.name: filter[invoice_status]
parameters.description: Filter by invoice status: uninvoiced, partial, invoiced.

schema.description: Filter by invoice status: uninvoiced, partial, invoiced.

parameters.name: filter[order_status]
parameters.description: Filter by order status: draft, open, closed. Invoices are recorded against non-draft POs.

get.summary: Get the full PO with all relations — lines, existing invoices, and financial_lines (each with its id). Needed when the invoice bills freight/fees: invoice financial_lines must reference an existing PO financial line id.

put.summary: Add a financial line (freight, duties, fees) to the PO so it can be invoiced — needed when the invoice bills a charge the PO has no financial line for yet. CAUTION: financial_lines is a SYNC — any existing PO financial line omitted from the payload is REMOVED, so include every existing line (by id) plus the new one (no id). Confirm with the user before editing a PO.

financial_lines.description: The COMPLETE set of the PO's financial lines. Existing lines: { id, ... }. New line: { financial_line_type_id (resolve via GET /api/v2/financial-line-types — e.g. the cost-classification "Shipping" type for freight), description, quantity, amount, allocate_to_products, proration_strategy }. allocate_to_products + "cost_based" prorates the charge into product landed cost at receiving.

get.summary: Get the PO's lines optimized for invoice creation — each line's id (the purchase_order_line_id an invoice line references), product_id, description, quantity, received_quantity, amount (PO unit cost), and discount_rate.

List purchase invoices — use before creating to catch a duplicate (same supplier invoice number) and to see what is already invoiced on the PO. filter[...] fields support operators like .is and .contains.

post.summary: Create the purchase invoice linked to a purchase order. Either purchase_invoice_lines or financial_lines must be provided; invoice lines must belong to the PO and must not be fully invoiced.

purchase_order_id.description: The purchase order this invoice bills (from find-purchase-order).

supplier_invoice_number.description: The supplier's own invoice number, exactly as printed on the document.

purchase_invoice_date.description: The invoice date printed on the document (ISO-8601). Required — a 422 without it.

due_date.description: Payment due date — from the document, or invoice date + the terms' net days.

status.description: Invoice status on creation — the allowed values are "unpaid", "paid", and "partially_paid"; use "unpaid" (the docs' "open" is rejected with a 422). Payment states are reached by recording payments, not by setting them here.

currency_id.description: Currency id — omit to use the PO's currency. Only set when the invoice is genuinely in a different currency, and resolve the id first (don't guess).

currency_rate.description: Conversion rate to the account base currency, when overriding currency.

tags.description: Array of string tags for filtering/reporting.

purchase_invoice_lines.description: Product lines. Each: { purchase_order_line_id (from get-po-lines-for-invoice), quantity_invoiced (must not exceed the line's uninvoiced remainder), unit_price }. unit_price is the GROSS price — the PO line's discount_rate is applied automatically, prorated to the invoiced quantity — so an invoice showing "90.25 less 15%" is passed as 90.25, not the net. Required unless financial_lines is provided.

financial_lines.description: Non-product charges being invoiced (freight, duties, fees). Each requires: id (an EXISTING financial line id from get-purchase-order — a 422 if missing), quantity, amount, AND link_type: "App\\Models\\PurchaseOrder" (a 422 "Financial line must be linked to a purchase order" without it). Required unless purchase_invoice_lines is provided.

post.summary: Upload the source invoice document to the recorded invoice as multipart/form-data. PDF, DOC/DOCX, PNG, JPG up to 20 MB. If the account has Invoice OCR auto-scan enabled a PDF is queued for OCR; if the invoice is synced to QuickBooks/Xero the file is forwarded there.

file.description: The file to attach (multipart form field).

category.description: Document category: invoice, payment_proof, or other (default). Use "invoice" for the source document.

get.summary: Verify the recorded invoice: per-PO-line comparison of ordered vs received vs invoiced quantities (qty_match_status: match, over_invoiced, under_invoiced — evaluated across all invoices and credits on the PO) and unit-price variance vs the PO.
List the account's payment types (id, name — e.g. Bank Transfer, Credit Card) to resolve payment_type_id before recording a payment. Scope settings:read.

post.summary: Record a payment that has already been made against the invoice. Amount must not exceed the remaining balance; negative amounts record refunds. Only records the fact — it moves no money.

payment_type_id.description: Payment type id (from list-payment-types). Don't invent it.

amount.description: Amount paid, in the invoice currency. Must not exceed the remaining balance.

payment_date.description: Date the payment was made (ISO-8601). Defaults to today if omitted.

currency_id.description: Currency id — omit to use the invoice's currency.
